issues.translation_quote: IRS
issues.justification: ОБХС is the Soviet anti-embezzlement/economic crimes police. 'IRS' is an anachronistic American tax agency and loses the joke about the crooks mistaking 'yes' for a police unit.

issues.source_quote: Тики так! Как стемнеет, будем брать!
issues.translation_quote: Tick-tock! Once it's dark, we grab it!
issues.justification: 'Тики-так' is a thieves' slang word for 'okay/fine'. 'Tick-tock' makes no sense and the later vocabulary lesson ('Good? - Tick-tock') loses its meaning. 'Tiki-tak' rendered as slang for 'OK' is needed.

issues.translation_quote: A beer hall? - Puke parlor.
issues.justification: The glossary of thieves' slang is rendered inconsistently. Later the same terms ('Редиска','нехороший человек') are glossed in the Russian but the English uses 'Radish' without explaining the in-joke of vegetable-as-insult; the 'Фрей-фея' (fraier) item is transliterated nonsensically and its meaning is lost.

issues.translation_quote: Frey-fey, right: Frey-fey.
issues.justification: This is the slang 'фраер' (sucker) distorted by a character who forgot it. Untranslated and meaningless to English viewers; the joke is lost.

issues.source_quote: Это тебе не мелочь по карманам тырить! Автомашину куплю с магнитофоном
issues.translation_quote: A shiny sharkskin suit
issues.justification: 'Костюм с отливом' means a shiny-fabric suit, here sharkskin is a plausible rendering, but 'Попался! За Доцента!' context (a beating of an informer) is flattened; 'Gotcha! That's for the Professor!' is acceptable. Main problem: the segment is jumbled by the mishandled 'Тики так'.

issues.source_quote: Нам не страшен серый волк, серый волк, серый волк...
issues.translation_quote: Who's afraid of the big bad wolf, big bad wolf, big bad wolf...
issues.justification: Culturally substituted Disney song is a creative choice, but the later parodic piglet-verse ('я в поросятах знаю толк') is rendered as 'I know a thing or two about piglets', losing the rhyme and the children's-song playfulness.

issues.source_quote: Давай червонец, керосинку буду покупать. - Примус очень худой - пожар может быть.
issues.translation_quote: Give tenner, I go buy kerosene stove. - Primus very bad - can be fire.
issues.justification: Broken pidgin English imposes a foreign-speaker voice on Russian that is merely colloquial. Vasya's speech is normal thieves' slang; only the later 'Эй, гражданина!' street bit is deliberate pidgin. The same broken style appears in 'Who put old woman in well?' and 'Where he go?', which misrepresents characters' voices.

issues.source_quote: Хмыренок! Деточка, а вам не кажется, что ваше место возле параши?
issues.translation_quote: Khmyr, buddy! Sweetie, don't you think your bunk's by the slop bucket?
issues.justification: The fellow inmate is deliberately mocking and insulting a newcomer; 'buddy' and 'sweetie' soften the prison taunt, and 'Хмыренок' (little Khmyr, a derogatory diminutive) is mistranslated as the name Khmyr.

issues.translation_quote: I'll rip your jaw off!
issues.justification: Acceptable, but the repeated gag 'Пасть, пасть...' later is rendered 'Jaw, jaw...', which does not work as a mocking echo. Also 'моргалы выколю' as 'gouge your peepers out' is fine. Minor loss only.

issues.source_quote: Те сидят там, в Средней Азии, а этот под Москвой.
issues.translation_quote: Those two are in Central Asia, he's outside Moscow.
issues.justification: Source speaks of those (several) who are sitting; 'two' is an invented number. Also 'им дали по 4 года' makes sense, but 'Those two' misidentifies the group.

issues.translation_quote: Bunks. You need to take the best spot.
issues.justification: Context is okay, but 'Отдавайте пиджак... Против бритвы - пиджак и брюки' and the chess game: 'Ходи лошадью' fine. More serious: 'Хмыренок' and 'Никола Питерский' are rendered 'Nikola from Piter', leaving an unexplained slang for St Petersburg.

issues.translation_quote: I died.
issues.justification: The preceding line asks whether the wife died; the answer in the source is 'Я умер' immediately after a joke context, but the translation adds nothing. The greater problem: 'Нету.' - 'Gone.' fine. Retain as minor only.

issues.translation_quote: Playing loves-me-loves-me-not in here
issues.justification: Acceptable adaptation, but 'Обзовись!' is rendered 'Swear it!' and 'Век воли не видать' as 'May I never see freedom' is a stiff literal rendering of a thieves' oath.

issues.translation_quote: Those two are in Central Asia
issues.justification: Number invented and awkward.

issues.source_quote: Нехороший человек, Косой, злой, как собака. Продаст, слышь, Доцент, сразу расколется.
issues.translation_quote: He'll sell us out, hear me, Professor, he'll crack right away.
issues.justification: Fine, but the running gag 'Нехороший человек' is rendered 'bad person' stiffly rather than a childish euphemism like 'not a nice man'.

issues.translation_quote: Sort of.
issues.justification: 'Вроде' here means 'it seems / apparently', not 'sort of'; the humor of the thieves posing as kindergarten heads is dulled.

issues.translation_quote: It is an utterly unique archaeological treasure.
issues.justification: 'Utterly unique' is awkward; 'one of a kind' or 'absolutely unique' would be more natural.

issues.translation_quote: Professor, he won't lie down!
issues.justification: 'Доцент' is a specific academic rank (Associate Professor) and also the criminal's nickname; later 'Assistant Professor' is used inconsistently for the same word ('The Assistant Professor came'), breaking the nickname consistency.

issues.translation_quote: Well done! So clean and tidy.
issues.justification: Fine, but 'Электричество кончилось' rendered as "'Lectricity's run out" adds an unmotivated dialect marker; the original is the standard cinema-hall joke 'Кина не будет'.

issues.translation_quote: Dinner is served. Sit down and stuff your faces, please.
issues.justification: Acceptable, but 'Кудай-то он?' rendered 'Where he go?' again introduces pidgin.

issues.translation_quote: Fitness greetings!
issues.justification: Literal rendering of a Soviet catchphrase 'Fizkult-privet' sounds odd in English; no flavor of era is conveyed.

issues.translation_quote: Brilliant!
issues.justification: Acceptable. The line 'Так бы и сказал...' rendered 'Should've just said so...' is fine.

issues.translation_quote: Tell me, how much does this helmet weigh?
issues.justification: Acceptable; but 'Тяжелая шапочка' as 'Heavy little hat' loses nothing. Dropped.

issues.source_quote: Вы Ваши 20 рублей положите в эту тумбочку
issues.translation_quote: Put your 20 rubles in this cabinet
issues.justification: 'Тумбочка' is a bedside table/nightstand; 'cabinet' is imprecise.

issues.translation_quote: Politeness is a thief's best weapon...
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: She won't squeal.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Те сидят там, в Средней Азии
issues.translation_quote: Those two
issues.justification: Repeated; duplicate of earlier.

issues.translation_quote: I thought you were dead
issues.justification: Fine.
